meta.title: Present Perfect Continuous Tenses
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Present Perfect Continuous Tenses themed around pets
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Present Perfect Continuous tense paired with topics like gerunds, relative clauses, passive voice, quantifiers, prepositions, and more, all within familiar pet contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: My golden retriever _____ his favorite toys under the sofa all week, and he _____ finding new hiding spots.

A.text: has been hiding / has been enjoying

B.text: have been hiding / have been enjoying

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. The singular subject 'retriever' requires 'has been hiding', and 'enjoy' is always followed by a gerund ('enjoying').
explanation.concept: Singular agreement in Present Perfect Continuous and verbs requiring gerund complements
explanation.formula: Singular subject + has been + verb-ing; subject + has been + enjoying + verb-ing
examples: The cat has been chasing the laser, and she has been loving every minute of it.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with subject-verb agreement. 'Cats' is plural, requiring 'have been'. 'Dog' is singular, requiring 'has been'.
explanation.concept: Correct auxiliary verbs for plural and singular subjects in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Plural subject + have been + verb-ing; singular subject + has been + verb-ing
examples: The birds have been singing, while the cat has been sleeping.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: I have been looking _____ my lost hamster _____ three hours, but I haven't found him yet.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Looking' is followed by 'for' when searching, and 'for' is used with a duration of time ('three hours').
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage with phrasal verbs and time expressions
explanation.formula: Have/has been looking for + noun + for + period of time
examples: I have been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous and Present Perfect Passive tenses with quantifiers. 'Many of the puppies' is plural, requiring 'have been'. 'Much of the mud' is uncountable and singular, requiring 'has been'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Quantifiers + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Agreement with plural and uncountable quantifiers in perfect tenses
explanation.formula: Many of + plural noun + have been + verb-ing; much of + uncountable noun + has been + past participle
examples: Many of the items have been sold, but much of the stock has been kept.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: My parrot _____ constantly _____ at the mirror, and it refuses _____ to stop.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with adverbs of frequency and infinitive verb patterns. 'Has been squawking' is the correct continuous form, and 'refuse' is followed by a to-infinitive ('to try').
explanation.concept: Continuous forms with adverbs and verbs requiring infinitive complements
explanation.formula: Subject + has/have been + constantly + verb-ing; subject + refuses + to-infinitive
examples: He has been constantly talking, and he refuses to stop.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with non-defining relative clauses and subject-verb agreement. 'Vet' is singular, requiring 'who is'.
explanation.concept: Singular agreement in relative clauses modifying the subject of a Present Perfect Continuous action
explanation.formula: Singular noun, who + is + verb-ing, + says + that + it + has been + verb-ing
examples: The doctor, who is treating the patient, says that he has been improving.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Since we adopted the rescue dog, he _____ constantly _____ at the mail carrier, which _____ our neighbors.

A.text: has / been barking / has been annoying

B.text: have / been barking / have been annoying

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with time clauses and relative clauses. 'Since' triggers the perfect aspect, and 'has been barking' emphasizes the ongoing, repeated nature of the action up to the present.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Time Clauses + Relative Clauses
explanation.concept: Ongoing actions starting in the past and continuing to the present, affecting another subject
explanation.formula: Since + past event, subject + has been + verb-ing, which + has been + verb-ing
examples: Since it started raining, we have constantly been waiting inside, which has been frustrating.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with advanced comparatives and adverb placement. 'Smarter' is already comparative, so 'more' is redundant. The adverb 'always' must be placed between the auxiliary 'has' and 'been'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Advanced Comparatives + Adverb Placement
explanation.concept: Correct comparative forms and adverb placement in perfect continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + is + comparative adjective; singular subject + has + always + been + verb-ing
examples: He is faster than me, and he has always been running ahead.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The kitten _____ up the curtains all morning, and I _____ trying to get it down without making a loud noise.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with phrasal verbs and gerund patterns. 'Has been climbing' is the correct singular form. 'Have been trying' is the correct plural form, and 'without' is a preposition followed by a gerund ('making').
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Phrasal Verbs + Gerunds
explanation.concept: Gerunds required after prepositions in continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + has been + phrasal verb; subject + have been + trying + without + verb-ing
examples: He has been running up the hill, and I have been trying without screaming.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with modal verbs of deduction in the perfect form. Modal verbs ('must') are always followed by the base form 'have', never 'has'.
explanation.concept: Base form of 'have' after modal verbs in perfect constructions
explanation.formula: Subject + has been + verb-ing; subject + must not + have + past participle
examples: She has been working hard, so she must not have forgotten the deadline.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Although the turtle _____ in our family for a decade, it _____ a single leaf yet.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with adverbial clauses of concession and the Present Perfect tense. The singular subject 'turtle' requires 'has been living' and 'hasn't eaten'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Conjunctions + Present Perfect
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in concessive clauses and perfect tenses
explanation.formula: Although + singular subject + has been + verb-ing, it + has not + past participle
examples: Although the cat has been living here for years, it hasn't learned to fetch.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with discourse markers. 'Has been molting' is required to show an action that started in the past and continues to the present, leading to the current result ('requires').
explanation.concept: Using resultative discourse markers with present perfect continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + has been + verb-ing + time expression; therefore, + subject + present simple verb
examples: It has been raining heavily all day; therefore, we are staying indoors.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: I have been training _____ unique breed of dog, and it _____ a joy to own.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with article usage. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), so it correctly takes the indefinite article 'a', not 'an'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before words starting with a /j/ sound
explanation.formula: Have/has been + verb-ing + a + word starting with /j/ sound
examples: She has been building a unique portfolio.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with ellipsis. The auxiliary 'do' is used to avoid repeating the full verb phrase ('have been feeding the fish') for the plural subject 'I'.
explanation.concept: Omitting repeated verb phrases using auxiliary verbs
explanation.formula: Subject + has been + verb-ing + object, and + subject + do/does
examples: He has been washing the car on Saturdays, and I do on Sundays.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: We have decided _____ a senior cat, and we have been avoiding _____ our landlord about it yet.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect tense with verb patterns, contrasting with the Present Perfect Continuous. 'Decide' is followed by a to-infinitive ('to adopt'), and 'avoid' is followed by a gerund ('telling').
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Gerunds vs. Infinitives
explanation.concept: Specific verbs requiring infinitive or gerund complements
explanation.formula: Have/has decided + to-infinitive; have/has been avoiding + verb-ing
examples: We have decided to move, and we have been avoiding telling anyone.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense (used here incorrectly for a future arrangement, should be Present Continuous, but let's fix the agreement first: 'We have been taking' is grammatically correct for duration, but 'are taking' is better for future. Let's change the error to 'has been' -> 'have been' for agreement, or 'are taking' for future arrangement. Let's make it: 'We are taking... so we have been buying'. Let's adjust the segment to test Future Arrangement vs Present Perfect Continuous).
explanation.concept: Distinguishing between ongoing actions and fixed future plans
explanation.formula: Subject + are + verb-ing (future) + , so + subject + have been + verb-ing (ongoing preparation)
examples: We are meeting tomorrow, so we have been preparing all week.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The flock of birds _____ south every winter, but a number of them _____ behind and have been adapting to the cold.

explanation.text: This combines the Simple Present tense with subject-verb agreement for collective nouns and quantifiers, contrasting with the Present Perfect Continuous. 'Flock' is a singular collective noun, requiring 'flies'. 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb ('stay').
explanation.concept: Agreement with collective nouns and 'a number of'
explanation.formula: Singular collective noun + verb + s/es; a number of + plural noun + base verb
examples: The team plays well, but a number of fans complain.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with non-defining relative clauses and subject-verb agreement. 'Leash' is singular, so the main clause verb must be 'has finally snapped'.
explanation.concept: Present Perfect in relative clauses describing duration up to the present, with singular main clause agreement
explanation.formula: Singular noun, which + subject + have/has been + verb-ing, + has + past participle
examples: The car, which I have owned for years, finally broke down.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: The iguana has been relying _____ the heat lamp, and it has been accustomed _____ basking under it all day.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Relying' is followed by 'on', and 'accustomed' is followed by 'to'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs and adjectives
explanation.formula: Has been relying on + noun; has been accustomed to + verb-ing
examples: He has been relying on his friend, and he has been accustomed to helping others.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense in a conditional structure. 'Has been wagging' emphasizes the duration of the action leading up to the present/future result 'will be'.
explanation.concept: Using Present Perfect Continuous in 'if' clauses to show duration leading to a result
explanation.formula: If + subject + has been + verb-ing + time, subject + will be + adjective
examples: If you have been studying all night, you will be tired.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The exotic fish _____ currently _____ by the aquarium staff, and the tanks _____ cleaned daily.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous passive voice with subject-verb agreement, contrasting with the Present Perfect Continuous context. 'Fish' (plural here) requires 'are being fed'. 'Tanks' is plural, requiring 'are being'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Passive Voice + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Correct past participle forms and plural agreement in passive voice
explanation.formula: Plural subject + are being + past participle
examples: The rooms are being cleaned right now.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect and Present Perfect Continuous tenses with quantifiers. 'Kittens' is a countable plural noun, requiring 'have found' (Present Perfect for completion). 'Population' is treated as an uncountable/singular concept here, requiring 'has been remaining' (or 'has remained').
explanation.concept: Countable vs. uncountable quantifiers and tense selection
explanation.formula: Many of + plural countable noun + have + past participle; much of + uncountable noun + has been + verb-ing
examples: Many of the books have sold, but much of the work has been remaining.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Rarely _____ the cat sleep on the floor; she has been _____ the highest shelf for weeks.

explanation.text: This combines the Simple Present tense with negative adverbial inversion and the Present Perfect Continuous. 'Rarely' triggers inversion ('does the cat sleep'). 'Has been preferring' is the correct continuous form.
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with negative adverbs and continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Rarely + auxiliary + subject + base verb; subject + has been + verb-ing
examples: Never does he arrive late; he has been leaving early for weeks.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous and Present Perfect Continuous tenses with gerund verb patterns. Both 'considering' and 'dreading' must be followed by a gerund ('getting', 'handling'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Have/has been + dreading + verb-ing
examples: I am considering moving, but I have been dreading packing.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the cleft sentence.
data.question: It _____ the veterinarian who _____ the most accurate diagnosis for my pet, which has been suffering for weeks.

explanation.text: This combines the Simple Present tense with cleft sentences for emphasis, alongside a Present Perfect Continuous relative clause. 'It is' emphasizes the subject, and the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular 'veterinarian', requiring 'makes'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in it-cleft structures with continuous relative clauses
explanation.formula: It + is + singular noun + who/that + present simple verb, which + has been + verb-ing
examples: It is the teacher who explains the concept clearly, which has been helping the students.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous with modal verbs of deduction in the perfect continuous form. Modal verbs ('must', 'can't') are always followed by the base form 'have', never 'has'.
explanation.concept: Base form of 'have' after modal verbs in perfect continuous constructions
explanation.formula: Subject + must/can't + have + been + verb-ing
examples: He must have been working all night.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: As the puppy grows, it _____ more energetic, and its tricks _____ increasingly complex.

A.text: has been becoming / have been becoming

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with conjunctions of time to describe changing situations over a period leading to the present. 'Has been becoming' and 'have been becoming' emphasize ongoing development.
explanation.concept: Describing changing situations and trends with 'as' using perfect continuous
explanation.formula: As + subject + verb + s/es, subject + has/have been + becoming + adjective
examples: As the weather has been getting colder, the days have been becoming shorter.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect passive voice with time clauses, contrasting with the Present Perfect Continuous. The past participles 'washed' and 'trimmed' are required after 'has/have been'.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Passive Voice + Time Clauses
explanation.concept: Correct past participle forms in Present Perfect passive
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + has/have been + past participle
examples: By the time we arrive, the food will have been eaten.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Not only _____ the dog been eating my shoes, but he _____ also been digging up the garden.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Perfect Continuous tense with 'not only... but also' inversion. 'Has' is required for the singular subject 'dog' in both clauses.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Not Only ... But Also
explanation.concept: Subject-auxiliary inversion with 'not only' in perfect continuous tenses
explanation.formula: Not only + has/have + subject + been + verb-ing, but + subject + has/have + also + been + verb-ing
examples: Not only has she been studying, but she has also been working.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines negative adverbial inversion with the Past Perfect Continuous tense. 'Little did I know' sets the past context, so the continuous action preceding it must be Past Perfect Continuous ('had been hiding'), not Present Perfect Continuous.
explanation.topic: Present Perfect Continuous + Inversion + Sequence of Tenses
explanation.concept: Adjusting perfect continuous tenses to match the past context of inverted adverbials
explanation.formula: Little + did + subject + know + that + subject + had been + verb-ing
examples: Little did I know that he had been waiting for hours.
